title: The Stanford d.school Cycle
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: design thinking and the Stanford d.school cycle.
final_note: Start with the user, not the idea.

concepts.def: Hasso Plattner Institute of Design at Stanford, founded 2005.
Understand the user through observation and interview.
Frame the design problem from user insights.
Generate many possible solutions without judgement.
Make a quick model to embody and test an idea.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Hasso Plattner Institute of Design at Stanford (the d.school) was founded in 2005 by David Kelley. Its five-stage design thinking framework spread globally through corporate and education adoption.
The cycle: Empathise (understand user), Define (frame problem), Ideate (generate solutions), Prototype (build to think), Test (learn from users).
The stages are not linear: testing returns to definition, prototyping reframes empathy. The point is to externalise thinking quickly and cheaply — fail in cardboard before you fail in steel.
